newsitem.title: USA: Biomet device banned from sale - court.
newsitem.headline: Biomet device banned from sale - court.

text.p: Biomet Inc said Tuesday that a U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit has denied the company's motion to stay an injunction, effectively banning Biomet from selling one of its orthopedic devices.

The injunction, effective immediately, prohibits the company from the future manufacture, use, promotion or sale of the finned version of the Mallory/Head acetabular cup in the United States, the company said in a statement.
The device accounts for a small portion of the total sales of the company's Mallory/Head System and represents less than one percent of the company's annual sales.
Biomet said it is vigorously pursuing its appeal before the Federal Circuit. It expects the court to issue its final decision on the appeal sometime in early 1998.

In January 1996, an initial $55 million jury award was made to plaintiff Raymond Tronzo who had sued Biomet alleging patent infringement and other violations of state laws. A judge reduced the award to $33.8 million in August 1996.
Biomet designs, develops, makes and markets products used primarily by orthopedic medical specialists in both surgical and non-surgical therapy.
Shares of Biomet were trading off 1/8 at 14-1/2.
